name: Pigeon Blue
lede: Pigeon Blue is a muted, greyish blue from the German RAL paint standard, named for the slate-blue sheen on a pigeon's neck feathers rather than its plain grey body.

sections.title: A bird's sheen, not its body
sections.body:
Our library catalogues this color as RAL 5014, from the RAL industrial color standard first published in Germany in 1927 [1]. Most of a pigeon's plumage is a flat grey, but the iridescent feathers around its neck shift between green and this kind of dusty blue-violet depending on the angle of the light, which is the likelier source of the name [1]. The ISCC-NBS system would call its block "pale purplish blue"; in Munsell it reads 5.2PB 5.1/4.3 [1].

The nearest named colors in our data are [[tyrian-blue|Tyrian Blue]], 2.9 CIEDE2000 units away, and [[light-tyrian-blue|Light Tyrian Blue]], 3.7 units away, with [[madder-blue|Madder Blue]] and [[shadow-blue|Shadow Blue]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Pigeon Blue appears in 223 of our 23,781 paintings, about 0.94 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 112, more common than 61 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 17 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.6 times the expected rate for that century, and in the 1840s decade specifically at 2.2 times expected [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, present in half of the 112 paintings where it carries real area [2].

The earliest match is dated 1405, in a work by Spinello Aretino — 522 years before RAL's 1927 record of the name, as photographed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. No single painter stands out against the museum baseline, though the Danish landscapist Peter Christian Skovgaard uses it most often among painters in our archive, in 4 of his 38 works here [2].
